flag_note: Tone Machines Blog documents a November 1967 Japan Music Trades advertisement in which the Greco No. 35 Fuzz Booster is the same wedge form as the Sekova Wedge Fuzz. This establishes a direct period Greco-to-wedge-fuzz connection, but the source explicitly leaves open whether Nisshin Onpa was already manufacturing pedals in 1967. Keep Nisshin as a high-priority factory lead rather than a confirmed manufacturer for No. 35.

builder: Nisshin Onpa Co., Ltd. / Aria / Greco
model_or_product: Pre-Maxon No.57-59 / No.83 fuzz and fuzz-wah families
flag_note: ToneHome states that first-series Ibanez effects were mainly manufactured by Maxon/Nisshin Onpa and that some products predate the Maxon name, when Nisshin Onpa sold unbranded fuzz and fuzz-wah pedals to companies including Aria and Greco. It specifically notes the No.57-59 Standard Pedals and No.83 New Fuzz can be found with Aria and Greco branding. Preserve Nisshin as the physical manufacturer and Aria/Greco as marketed identities for the supported pre-Maxon family; do not back-project that proof automatically onto every 1960s wedge fuzz.

Tone Machines Blog argues the Greco No.35, Sekova wedge fuzzes and Shaftesbury-type wedges belong to a common Japanese OEM family, with at least four enclosure/power variants and an earliest likely date around 1967. The physical factory remains unresolved and should not be inferred from family resemblance alone.
